Per-test significance level for FDR-controlled sample-size planning

Source: R/tidyMS_power_fdr.R
fdr_sig_level.Rd

Convert a target false discovery rate and average power into the per-test significance level used by an ordinary two-sided t-test. Pass the result to stats::power.t.test(), lfq_power_t_test_proteins(), or lfq_power_t_test_quantiles().

Usage

fdr_sig_level(fdr = 0.05, pi0 = 0.95, power = 0.8)

Arguments

fdr

one target false discovery rate, strictly between zero and one.

pi0

one assumed proportion of truly null features, strictly between zero and one; it is not estimated from the pilot.

power

one target average power among non-null features, strictly between zero and one.

Value

The scalar per-test significance level \(\alpha_* = power \times fdr \times (1-pi0) / (pi0 \times (1-fdr))\). Combinations giving a significance level outside (0, 1) are rejected.

Details

The Jung/Liu–Hwang planning relationship assumes independent tests or an adequate approximation under weak dependence, and many tested features. It controls the expected false-discovery proportion under the assumed null fraction and effect distribution, not the realized FDR of every experiment. All sample sizes are per group in a balanced two-group design with equal within-group variances.

References

Jung SH (2005). Sample size for FDR-control in microarray data analysis. Bioinformatics 21:3097–3104. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bti456 . Liu P, Hwang JTG (2007). Quick calculation for sample size while controlling false discovery rate with application to microarray analysis. Bioinformatics 23:739–746. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btl664 .

See also

Other stats: INTERNAL_FUNCTIONS_BY_FAMILY, compute_pooled(), lfq_power_t_test_proteins(), lfq_power_t_test_quantiles(), null_split_check(), plot_stat_density(), plot_stat_density_median(), plot_stat_violin(), plot_stat_violin_median(), plot_stdv_vs_mean(), pooled_variance_explained(), power_fdr_prior_n(), summarize_stats(), summarize_variance_explained()

Examples

alpha <- fdr_sig_level(fdr = 0.05, pi0 = 0.9, power = 0.8)
alpha
#> [1] 0.004678363
ceiling(stats::power.t.test(delta = 1, sd = 1, sig.level = alpha, power = 0.8)$n)
#> [1] 29
